liebermann.notes: One hand c. 1125–30, then belonging to St Paul's, London; bound in front is a 16th-century copy of II–III Edgar from A. Contains Blas, Forf, Hu, I Atr, AGu, EGu, II As, Af–Ine, I–II Cnut (with a 16th-century copy of I Cn 17,1 from A), I–II Ew, I–II Em, Swer, Wif, Wer, Becwæð, II Atr, Duns, Rect, Ger and, in a 12th-century hand, a list of ship-levies from London church estates; leaves are lost in several places, and B followed an 11th-century collection (cf. hb).

wormald.liebermann_date: one hand, c. 1125–30; a 16th-century copy bound in front; p. 107 another hand, 12th century
wormald.wormald_date: s. xi/xii (p. 165, Table 4.1); main scribe wrote 'at the turn of the eleventh and twelfth centuries' (p. 233); shipmen list and genealogy added s. xii¹ (p. 229)
wormald.wormald_origin: St Paul's, London (p. 165): the near-contemporary list of shipmen (pp. 107–8) concerns St Paul's estates; a corrector who may be the shipmen-list scribe had the exemplar, implying the MS was written at St Paul's (pp. 230, 234 and n. 285); Bishop Maurice of London (ex-royal chaplain and chancellor) likely interested (p. 236). Had left St Paul's by s. xiii (French text p. 5; note of 'Matildis ... soror magistri Roberti ... de Abbend', p. 29, perhaps Robert of Abingdon) (p. 230 and n. 268). Annotated by Talbot; then in Parker's circle, who paginated it in red crayon, wrote a contents list and added transcripts of II–III Eg (from Harley 55(A)) and I Cn (from Harley 55(B)) (p. 230 and nn. 266–7).
wormald.laws: Preliminary quire: II–III Eg (s. xvi² transcript). Quire 1: Blas (from 3; second half), Forf, Hu, I Atr, AGu (B² text, p. 6), EGu, II As (to 6, incomplete). Quires 2–3: Af–Ine (from Af El 3; leaf lost after p. 22 = Af 41–43), Blas (to 3; first half). Inserted quire: I Cn to 17:1 (s. xvi² transcript). Quires 4–7: I–II Cn (from I Cn 14:2; with I Cn 'epilogue' found only here, p. 231 n. 271), I–II Ew, I–II Em, Swer, AGu (B¹ text, pp. 83–4), Wif, Wer, charm for stolen cattle (struck through), Becwæð (Hit becweð), II Atr (with 'Appendix', clauses 8–9:4), Duns, Rect, Ger. At least three quires lost (before quire 2, after quire 1, after quire 7).

wormald.other_contents: Only legal texts, plus later additions: St Paul's 'shipmen' list (s. xii¹) and a truncated West Saxon genealogical regnal list (s. xii¹), pp. 107–8; French text p. 5 (s. xiii); Latin/French text in lower margins pp. 48–52 (s. xii/xiii). Heavy corrections by the scribe and at least two other hands; Alfred–Ine and Cnut re-rubricated / divided into chapters by later hands.
wormald.overview: A small book containing only laws, written around 1100 mainly by one scribe and owned (probably also made) at St Paul's, London; Wormald thinks it perhaps the earliest of the three large law collections of the early twelfth century. It is built from ready-made groups of texts (Alfred–Ine followed by Blas, Forf, Hundred and I Atr; Edward and Edmund with Swerian, Wif, Wer, a cattle charm and Becwæð; II Atr with Dunsæte, Rectitudines and Gerefa), and it alone preserves II Æthelred in Old English and holds both Old English copies of Alfred–Guthrum. The main scribe's Old English is so faulty that Wormald suspects it was not his usual language, yet correctors and later rubricators worked to make the text usable; he links its interest in relations between English and Danes to the post-conquest regime and to Bishop Maurice of London.
wormald.liebermann_superseded: Liebermann dated the main hand c. 1125–30, whereas Wormald puts it at the turn of the eleventh and twelfth centuries (s. xi/xii); he also notes that corrections Liebermann called sixteenth-century are medieval, and that the Talbot note Liebermann took as proof of continued St Paul's ownership in the sixteenth century proves nothing (pp. 165, 233, 230 n. 268, 234 n. 285).
wormald.key_quote: Old English law was important enough to need copying by someone not competent to do so. (p. 236)
wormald.doubts: Ker, Catalogue no. 65. Wormald's siglum B = Liebermann's B. GUIDE: Wormald's Table 4.6 (image checked) labels the AGu copy on p. 6 'B²' and the one on pp. 83–4 'B¹'. RESOLVED: this matches Liebermann — in the site's AGu XML Liebermann's text with the red heading 'Ælfredes laga cyninges' is B2, and Wormald says the second copy (pp. 83–4) lacks a rubric (p. 236), so Liebermann's B2 is the first copy in manuscript order (p. 6). The guide's labels B1 = 'first copy', B2 = 'second copy' are therefore reversed and should be corrected. GUIDE: the guide's date 'c. 1125–30' should be updated to s. xi/xii (Wormald). Guide's laws list omits that II As and Af–Ine are incomplete and that II–III Eg and part of I Cn are 16th-century transcripts. Nowell had already found the quire after quire 1 lost ('Desunt nonnulla' in BL Add. MS 43703 at the break in II As, p. 230 n. 265); suggestion that Nowell/Lambarde saw a fuller MS is doubted (ibid.). Bishop Maurice: no dates given by Wormald. || Passing mention only (n. 97, image checked). Guide says B has a 16th-century copy of II–III Eg from A bound in front and a 16th-century copy of I Cn 17,1 from A — consistent with Wormald. Passing remarks (from MEL p. 185 n. 97): Mentioned here only for the early modern supplements: the texts of Edgar and Cnut copied into the manuscript both derive from Harley 55, but were taken at different times, which suggests the two parts of Harley 55 were not then together. Main discussion is at p. 230.

verify_notes: Overview: 'probably not a native speaker' too strong (Wormald: a 'suspicion', p. 234) — softened; ownership wording aligned with p. 230/234 (written at or soon procured by St Paul's, probably written there).
Doubt on AGu B1/B2 resolved against the site's AGu XML: guide labels reversed.

laws_note.text: II–III Eg and I Cn to 17:1 are sixteenth-century transcripts bound in; II As and Af–Ine are incomplete through lost leaves; the book also has a charm for stolen cattle. Of the two copies of AGu, the one on pp. 83–4 is Liebermann’s B (this site’s B1) and the one on p. 6 his B 2 (Gesetze I, p. 126; Wormald p. 236).
